Fixed. Root cause confirmed: audit_entries.id (migration 001) was a global PRIMARY KEY but next_audit_id() generates per-design-scoped ids (AUD-001, AUD-002, ... first/second entry FOR THAT DESIGN) -- once any design claimed AUD-001, DesignStore.save()'s INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (keyed on id alone) silently dropped every other design's own AUD-001. Confirmed live against real Postgres before fixing: 6 designs, only 11 total audit_entries rows, only 1 design owned AUD-001. Fix (migration 036, down_revision 035): composite PRIMARY KEY (design_id, id) -- id only needs to be unique within its own design, which is exactly the scope it's already generated at; the AUD-NNN id format/pattern (ADP-SPEC-001's AuditEntryId) is untouched. DesignStore.save()'s on_conflict_do_nothing index_elements updated from ['id'] to ['design_id','id'] to match. Same migration backfills every row the bug had been silently dropping, reconstructed from each design's own canonical audit_log (design_versions.content at its current_version -- the JSONB copy was never affected by this bug, only the relational mirror was). Applied to the real local dev DB: audit_entries went from 11 rows to 179 across 45 real designs (41 now correctly own their own AUD-001). Verified live post-fix that two different designs writing AUD-001 in the same process no longer collide (both persisted). ruff/mypy clean on all 3 changed files; full non-integration suite (1642 tests) passes unchanged -- this bug only manifests against real Postgres (SQLite-backed unit/contract fixtures don't exercise the ON CONFLICT path), so verification was done directly against the live local Postgres rather than the Docker-gated integration suite (Docker unavailable in this environment, same constraint as every other spec this session). Found and filed a separate, unrelated pre-existing bug while verifying (tests/integration/test_store.py::test_mutation_rolls_back_without_audit's own premise doesn't hold against real Postgres) as ADP-4qv rather than fixing it here -- out of scope for this bead. Files: src/adp/store/migrations/versions/036_audit_entries_composite_pk.py (new), src/adp/store/records.py, src/adp/store/store.py. Not yet committed -- awaiting user direction on commit/push/PR per this repo's conservative git policy.

Fixed. Resolved the open design question: a same-design audit-entry id collision should raise and roll back, but ONLY when it's a genuine collision (differing content) -- legitimate re-accumulation (a save re-submitting an already-persisted, unchanged entry, which is the normal case since audit_log always carries the full accumulated history) must stay a silent no-op, or every real save would start failing. Confirmed both a design bug AND a test bug: DesignStore.save()'s audit_entries insert used ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keyed on (design_id, id) with no way to distinguish the two cases; separately, test_mutation_rolls_back_without_audit's own dup_entry used id='AUD-DUP' / a sibling test used 'AUD-T01', both of which fail AuditEntryId's '^AUD-\d{3}$' pattern at construction time -- neither test could ever have run, confirming this whole file has never actually executed (Docker-gated, unavailable in this environment, same constraint as every other spec this session). Fix: DesignStore.save() (src/adp/store/store.py) now uses ON CONFLICT (design_id, id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE <any of actor/action/affected_entity/summary/timestamp/origin differs>, exploiting the existing append-only trigger (deny_audit_mutation(), migration 001) as the raise mechanism -- when the WHERE predicate is false (unchanged re-submission) no UPDATE is attempted, silent no-op as before; when true (genuine collision) Postgres attempts the UPDATE, the trigger unconditionally rejects it, and the resulting DBAPIError is caught and re-raised as a new typed adp.store.AuditIntegrityError (added to the StoreError hierarchy and store/__init__.py's exports, mirroring the existing SchemaValidationError/ConcurrencyConflictError pattern -- not wired into any router, matching how those two aren't either). Rewrote test_mutation_rolls_back_without_audit to use valid AUD-NNN ids and a genuine content-differing collision (asserts AuditIntegrityError + version count stays 1); added test_audit_reinsertion_of_unchanged_entry_is_noop as the explicit contrast case; fixed test_audit_trigger_fires_on_delete's invalid 'AUD-T01' id inline (trivial, same file, same root cause) and scoped its delete by design_id too now that id alone isn't a unique key post-ADP-a64. Verified live against the real local Postgres (integration suite itself still can't run locally -- Docker unavailable): both the genuine-collision-raises-and-rolls-back path and the legitimate-re-accumulation-succeeds path confirmed working exactly as coded, test data cleaned up afterward (audit_entries count back to 179, designs back to 45, matching ADP-a64's own post-fix baseline). ruff/mypy clean; full non-integration suite still 1642 passed (unchanged -- this bug/fix, like ADP-a64's, only manifests against real Postgres's trigger+ON CONFLICT machinery, not SQLite fixtures). Files: src/adp/store/store.py, src/adp/store/__init__.py, tests/integration/test_store.py. Not yet committed -- awaiting user direction on commit/push/PR per this repo's conservative git policy; note this stacks on ADP-a64's own uncommitted migration 036 change (same audit_entries table, same conflict-target column list) so both should land together.

Fixed. Root cause was much broader than 'some existing test(s) leak state': db_session's own BEGIN/ROLLBACK isolation only covers writes made directly through the db_session object -- but the majority of integration tests instead write through a DesignStore (test_store.py's store fixture) or a real FastAPI app wired to its own separate engine (every *_api.py file's app/client fixtures, e.g. test_business_api.py, test_application_api.py, test_compliance_api.py, test_compliance_mappings_api.py, test_framework_legal_dates_api.py, test_strategy_compliance_links_api.py). Confirmed by direct code inspection: none of those fixtures' engines are ever wrapped in a transaction that gets rolled back -- every write through them is a real, permanent commit to the single session-scoped shared Postgres container, in file/test collection order. This is structural (built into most of the suite's fixture design from the start), not a single rogue test.

Fix: a new directory-wide, autouse  fixture in tests/integration/conftest.py truncates every public-schema table (except alembic_version) before each test runs, discovered dynamically via pg_tables so a future migration adding a table can't silently reopen this. TRUNCATE bypasses row-level triggers (unlike DELETE), so it doesn't trip audit_entries' append-only guard. Chose 'truncate before, not after' deliberately: a test that crashes mid-body still leaves the *next* test clean, at the cost of the *last* test's data lingering until the next session starts (a feature for post-failure debugging).

Two real implementation landmines found and resolved via direct experiment (not assumed) against this project's actual pytest-asyncio config (asyncio_mode=auto, session-scoped fixture/test loops):
1. An async autouse fixture applied file-wide breaks any plain sync  in the same file (pytest-asyncio raises PytestRemovedIn9Warning/error) -- confirmed by a minimal reproduction before touching the real suite. Fixed by giving the two DB-free/sync-test files (test_render_e2e.py, test_export_bundle.py) and the two files that deliberately use their own non-shared container for downgrade testing (test_migration_022.py, test_migration_023.py) a local no-op override of the same fixture name, which pytest resolves per-module.
2. Root cause found, real bug (not just e2e flakiness) -- fixed. DesignStore.next_design_id() (src/adp/store/store.py) computes 'max existing DSN-NNN + 1' via a plain SELECT with no lock spanning it and the later INSERT in create_design()'s call to store.save(). Confirmed reproducible against the real running backend: 5 concurrent POST /api/v1/designs all racing gave 4x 500 Internal Server Error (asyncpg.UniqueViolationError on design_versions_pkey); the flaky e2e symptom was this exact race between the 'Design creation via UI' test's own design POST and the very next describe block's beforeAll POST landing ~15ms apart, which is far closer together than sequential Playwright execution should allow but was confirmed via JSON reporter timestamps to actually happen.

Fix (src/adp/api/routers/designs.py create_design): retry loop (5 attempts) around next_design_id()+store.save(), catching both real failure shapes this race produces: (1) the common case, a raw sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError when the loser's design_versions INSERT collides head-on; (2) a narrower, initially-alarming case where our next_design_id() snapshot predates a competitor's commit for that same id, so store.save()'s own existing-design check sees it as an update rather than a create and would insert a spurious new version onto the competitor's design -- traced all the way through and confirmed SAFE: every freshly-constructed design's lone audit entry is always synthesized as 'AUD-001' regardless of the target id's real history, so it collides with that id's real committed AUD-001 and raises AuditIntegrityError, which rolls back the whole transaction (store.save() wraps it all in one session.begin()) including the spurious version insert. Both are retried transparently; exhausting all 5 attempts returns 503 (safe to retry) instead of a raw 500.

Verified: 5 rounds of 2-way and 3-way concurrent POSTs all succeed cleanly with the fix (0 failures); higher artificial concurrency (8-10 way) can still exhaust retries and surface a clean 503 under sustained contention -- an accepted, explicitly out-of-scope tradeoff for this fix (this bug is about the realistic ~2-way collision the e2e suite actually hit, not a thundering-herd production scenario; a real fix for that would need a DB sequence or advisory lock, bigger scope than this bug warrants). 3 new contract tests added (tests/contract/test_designs_api.py: retry-on-IntegrityError, retry-on-AuditIntegrityError, 503-after-exhausting-retries). Full flows.spec.ts fullstack e2e suite (real backend+DB) run 3x clean after the fix (was reproducing the collision on the very first run before the fix). ruff/mypy clean. Full backend unit+contract suite run (1657+3 tests) -- 3 pre-existing failures confirmed unrelated (LLM stub-vs-real-key tests, fail identically with this fix stashed out; caused by a real, valid ADP_LLM_API_KEY in the local .env, an existing environmental condition, not a regression from this change).

Note: could not clean up the synthetic designs created while reproducing this (RaceTest*/Pair-*/Triple-* via direct curl) -- there is no delete-design endpoint anywhere in the API, and audit_entries has a BEFORE DELETE/UPDATE trigger (deny_audit_mutation()) enforcing its append-only/immutable invariant, so even a raw SQL delete isn't a safe option. This matches the pre-existing pattern of every historical E2E-* design in this same dev DB never being cleaned up either -- confirmed this is by design, not an oversight, before leaving it as-is.
